_limits: THE MANIFEST MAKES RECORDS DURABLE, NOT TRUE. A quote entered wrongly at creation time is preserved faithfully, hashed, and dated forever — initial verification is the single point of failure, and it has demonstrably failed once (col-prostate: a quote recorded as 'confirmed directly' that was never at the named source, evidenced by a Wayback snapshot predating the verification). The structural checks cannot reach that class; nothing can, except care at entry.
_ruling_statistics: Downgrade-to-illustrative works only for values with an honest illustrative home (colour). It does NOT work for statistics: a user reads '~92%' as fact regardless of labelling. For statistical claims the options are RE-SOURCE (durably-addressed) or REMOVE from the screen — no middle.
_backfill_method: Identifier backfill (2026-09-04): PubMed eutils esearch/esummary with a MULTI-FIELD AGREEMENT GATE — first-author surname + publication year + (journal when recorded) + topic-consistency, and EXACTLY ONE candidate may pass; ambiguous or partial matches are refused, never guessed. Backfilled identifiers carry method+date and DO NOT have the evidentiary weight of identifiers recorded at entry time: they assert 'this recorded metadata resolves uniquely to this paper', not 'this paper was verified to support the claim'. Triage semantics: status=no-match (author+year yields zero PubMed hits) is the strong entry-time-error signature (the Wang/Park case); status=no-field-match is NOT a defect list — it mixes common-surname retrieval misses, retmax truncation, and title-topic gate strictness, and means 'not auto-resolvable', nothing more. SWEEP 2 (2026-09-04, same gate, leakier-retrieval fixes user-specified after the Louis case): PubMed retmax raised 8->100 with the esearch total count recorded (count>100 = saturated, exhaustiveness cannot be claimed); topic terms placed IN the query (All Fields: title+abstract+MeSH) as well as the post-hoc title check, with the instrument recorded per entry (topic:title vs topic:query); Crossref added as a second engine (different index, fuzzy bibliographic matching); passers identity-deduped across engines by title-token Jaccard>=0.7 and the union must contain EXACTLY ONE paper. Residue subclasses replace no-field-match: ambiguous-2 (multiple genuine passers — several are two real same-author-same-year papers), saturated (query too big to sweep), zero-pass (candidates exist, none pass all fields).

On every backfill testable against an entry-time identifier, the >=3-field machinery went 4/4 correct (Jakob, Livasy, Luvhengo via sweep-1; Wippold via sweep-2) and A+Y-only went 2/2 wrong. RULE ADOPTED: automated backfill requires at least three agreeing fields; author+year+uniqueness alone is never sufficient. Every backfilled entry now carries fieldsChecked — the strength actually applied, not the strength specified. RULE SUPERSEDED (2026-09-04): the wrong-backfill census is CATEGORICAL, not a threshold result — all four wrong backfills in the no-journal class, zero in any journal-checked class. Minimum-three counted fields as fungible when the data says they are not: journal names are high-entropy and nearly impossible to match spuriously; topic is low-entropy, substring-prone, and was actively defective. JOURNAL IS NOW REQUIRED for automated backfill (author+year+journal at minimum; evidence: ~14% error rate in the no-journal class, 4/29). v2's 73% journal recall makes this affordable where v1's 44% would not have. Records without a journal anywhere on the line can only be resolved by a HUMAN title-read (fieldsChecked carries title:human), never automatically.
_polarity_guard: Polarity guard (.claude/citation_polarity.py, 2026-09-04, born from the Boutros failure class): a token-matching pass has no notion of a claim's polarity — an authorship correction, a "checked and NOT confirmed" caveat, and a straight assertion carry the same author-plus-year tokens. The guard classifies WINDOWS (corrective / caveated / clean) and its contract is flag-then-human-read: window-level regexes cannot tell a negated mention (Colombino) from its correction target (Jakob) two tokens later, so it never auto-acts. _epi_pass_contract: EPI-PASS VERDICT CONTRACT (ruled 2026-09-04): three states, not two — VERIFIED (the source supports the claim as shipped), FAILED (the source exists and contradicts or lacks the claim), and NOT-A-SOURCE-CLAIM (the mention cites a paper to say something ABOUT it, not to draw a fact FROM it: corrective mentions, mis-citer exhibits like Hu 2012, documented-unverifiable notes like Curtin 2005). A binary pass would check "does Hu 2012 contain 54/32/15", find no, and report a defect against a line that already says the figures are wrong — misreading corrective mentions in both directions. The polarity scan flags 36 windows (9 corrective, 27 caveated); every flagged window gets a human mention-level read that may assign NOT-A-SOURCE-CLAIM before any automated verify/fail verdict is recorded.
